title: Derived geometric-point direct image is global sections with its adjunction
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $Z$ any scheme and $h:Z\to s$ a morphism. Let $S_D:D(s_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)\to D(\mathbf Z)$ and $C_s$ be the termwise geometric-stalk and constant-complex functors of [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants]. Write $C_Z$ for the constant-complex functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf], $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ for the derived inverse/direct-image adjunction [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and $R\Gamma_Z=R\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},-)$ for derived global sections [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Let $\gamma:h^{-1}C_s\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z$ be the canonical pullback-of-constants comparison [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. There is a natural isomorphism
$$\beta_E:S_D Rh_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_ZE$$
for every $E\in D(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\mathbf Z)$. It is the isomorphism of right adjoints obtained by identifying the left adjoints $h^{-1}C_s$ and $C_Z$ through $\gamma$. More explicitly, let $\epsilon^s:C_sS_D\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit of the constant/stalk equivalence, $\epsilon^h:h^{-1}Rh_*\to\mathrm{id}$ the derived direct-image counit, and $\epsilon^Z:C_ZR\Gamma_Z\to\mathrm{id}$ the constant-section counit [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Then, naturally in $E$,
$$\epsilon^Z_E\circ C_Z(\beta_E)\circ\gamma_{S_D Rh_*E}
=\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E}).$$
For a sheaf $G$ in degree zero, $\beta_G$ on degree-zero cohomology is the canonical identification $S(h_*G)\cong(h_*G)(s)=G(Z)$, induced by inverse to the global-section-to-germ map on $s$. No properness, torsion or finiteness assumption is made.

proof.text:
Put $F=h^{-1}C_s$ and $G=S_D Rh_*$. The normalized equivalence of [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants] supplies $C_s\dashv S_D$ with the stated counit $\epsilon^s$. Compose its Hom bijection with that of $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ from [def-kun-projection-formula-map]:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(FM,E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_sM,Rh_*E)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,GE).$$
These are bijections natural in both variables, hence define $F\dashv G$. The inverse sends $a:M\to GE$ to
$$\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E})\circ F(a).$$
Indeed, apply the two inverse adjunction formulas successively. In particular its counit is $k_E=\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E}):FGE\to E$.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; composite counit computed by composing the two Hom bijections, as in categories.tex Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits.

proof.text: Use the canonical isomorphism $\gamma:F\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Z$ of [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Precomposition by $\gamma_M$ takes $\operatorname{Hom}(C_ZM,E)$ bijectively to $\operatorname{Hom}(FM,E)$; following this by Step 1 defines an adjunction $C_Z\dashv G$. Its inverse Hom bijection sends $a:M\to GE$ to $k_E\circ F(a)\circ\gamma_M^{-1}$. Naturality of $\gamma$ rewrites this as $k_E\circ\gamma_{GE}^{-1}\circ C_Z(a)$, so its counit is $\lambda_E=k_E\circ\gamma_{GE}^{-1}$. This also fixes which direction of the constants comparison is used.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and transport of its Hom bijection through the canonical pullback-of-constants comparison; explicit calculation supplied here.

proof.text:
The canonical constant-section adjunction of [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] is $C_Z\dashv R\Gamma_Z$ with counit $\epsilon^Z$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to this adjunction and the adjunction $C_Z\dashv G$ of Step 2. It gives a natural isomorphism $\beta:G\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_Z$, uniquely characterized by
$$\epsilon^Z_E\circ C_Z(\beta_E)=\lambda_E.$$
Precompose with $\gamma_{GE}$ and substitute the expression for $\lambda_E$. The two inverse constants comparisons cancel, giving exactly
$$\epsilon^Z_E\circ C_Z(\beta_E)\circ\gamma_{GE}=\epsilon^h_E\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon^s_{Rh_*E}).$$
Thus the isomorphism is the specified isomorphism of right adjoints, rather than merely an objectwise isomorphism. All these adjunctions are on unbounded derived categories, with no restriction on $h$ or $E$.

proof.text:
For an abelian sheaf $H$ on $s$, let $\rho_H:H(s)\to SH$ be the global-section-to-germ map of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. The constant-section adjunction [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] and the normalized constant/stalk equivalence give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A,H(s))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_sA,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(A,SH).$$
The second bijection sends $u$ to $S(u)\circ\eta_A$, where $\eta_A$ sends a constant to its germ [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants]. Under the first bijection, $u$ takes a constant $a$ to the corresponding global section and its restrictions: this follows directly from the sheafification defining $C_s$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Thus the composite sends $v:A\to H(s)$ to $\rho_H\circ v$. Taking $A=\mathbf Z$ proves that $\rho_H$ is a bijection, hence an isomorphism of abelian groups. Its naturality is the defining naturality of the germ map. By the direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $(h_*J)(s)=J(Z)$ for every abelian sheaf $J$ on $Z$.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point, with trivial Galois group; normalized constant-germ calculation using sites.tex Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf.

proof.text: Represent $E$ by a K-injective complex $I$ of abelian sheaves on $Z$, using [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist] with $R=\mathbf Z$. The recipes in [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] represent $GE$ by $S(h_*I)$ and $R\Gamma_ZE$ by $\Gamma(Z,I)$, respectively. The termwise equivalence in [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants] identifies its counit with the termwise ordinary counit. By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], ordinary counits also give the counits on homotopy categories. The right adjoints $h_*$ and $\Gamma_Z$ preserve K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since their left adjoints $h^{-1}$ and $C_Z$ are exact by the two adjunction definitions. Thus $h_*I$ and $\Gamma_ZI$ are K-injective too. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], all three Hom sets with these targets are computed on homotopy categories; consequently the canonical derived adjunctions in [def-kun-projection-formula-map] and [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] have counits represented by the ordinary evaluation counits on $I$. For the constants adjunction one can also apply the Hom bijection directly on complexes and then localize: its exact left adjoint is the termwise constant functor, as specified in the latter definition. These are computations on a chosen resolution, not an assertion that ordinary sections is exact.

proof.text: The inverses of Step 4's maps $\rho_{h_*I^q}:\Gamma(Z,I^q)\xrightarrow{\sim}S(h_*I^q)$ form a cochain isomorphism $b_I:S(h_*I)\to\Gamma(Z,I)$, since $\rho$ is natural. Check the equation of Step 3 on this representative, in each degree. A constant element $a\in S(h_*I^q)$ corresponds under $\rho^{-1}$ to a unique section $t\in(h_*I^q)(s)=I^q(Z)$. The normalized counit $C_sS(h_*I^q)\to h_*I^q$ sends the constant $a$ to $t$: applying the faithful stalk functor gives $a$, by the counit normalization of [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants] and the definition of $\rho$. Pulling this map back and applying the $h$-counit evaluates the section $t$ on $Z$. The other side first uses the canonical $\gamma$ of [lem-kun-pullback-constant], then $b_I$ to take $a$ to $t$, and then the constant-section counit, which evaluates the same section. Hence the two maps agree on constants and their restrictions, and therefore on their sheafifications [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Step 5's counit models give the derived equation. The uniqueness assertion of [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] now identifies the class of $b_I$ with $\beta_E$.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; termwise evaluation calculation of the displayed counit identity, with sites.tex Tag 0H7J for evaluation of constant sections.

proof.text: Now let $E=J[0]$ for a sheaf $J$ on $Z$. On a small representative of the etale site, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](1) give an injective resolution $J[0]\to I$ with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$. It is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so Step 6 applies. The additive left exactness of $h_*$ is part of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Evaluation of sheaf morphisms at $Z$ preserves their pointwise sums, so sections is additive; being the right adjoint in [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], preserves kernels by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] (apply it to the finite kernel diagram). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](2) gives the augmentation identifications $\mathcal H^0(h_*I)=h_*J$ and $\mathcal H^0\Gamma(Z,I)=J(Z)$. Exactness of $S$ [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants] gives $\mathcal H^0S(h_*I)=S(h_*J)$. Naturality of $\rho$ for $h_*J\to h_*I^0$ says that the square of the two augmentation maps with $\rho_{h_*J}$ and $\rho_{h_*I^0}$ commutes. Since the degree-zero boundaries are zero, passing to degree-zero kernels shows that $\mathcal H^0(b_I)=\rho_{h_*J}^{-1}$. This is precisely $S(h_*J)\cong(h_*J)(s)=J(Z)$, inverse to the global-section-to-germ map, as required. The bounded-below resolution here only computes the normalization for a sheaf; Steps 1-6 apply to arbitrary unbounded $E$.
